parts:
Hi Stan,

      I am working on the implementation of Neatest Neighborhood Gaussian Process (NNGP) in Stan. I wrote a test folder and here is the share link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0ByIcksYvjph9aS1GajdzY2dCWGc?usp=sharing.
The folder exceeds the limits for this group so I put it in the google driver. Please let me know if it is not accessible. It contains the synthetic data and codes for four different models. For more information, please check "readme" and "summary.pdf". Since it hasn't been completed yet, the summary report is still in editing. Welcome for suggestions for improving my code. I also posted two questions in the end of this topic. Thank you very much!


The following is file "Readme.txt" which gives a brief introduction of this folder:

# Introduction:

This is a test folder for implementing Full Gaussian process and Nearest 
Neighborhood Gaussian Process on spatial data in Stan. For more details 
about synthetic data, models, and simulation results, please refer to 
“summary.pdf”.  


# How to run the program:

The language interface to perform the analysis is Rstan. All the executable files 
are in subfolder “projects” and Stan codes are saved in subfolder “src”. To run 
the analysis, open R program in “projects” and set the working directory to be 
the path of this folder. R code in subfolder “projects” will load data and link 
Stan codes with a relative path. 


# Folder Structure:

data: Synthetic data and parameters for priors

projects:         Rstan codes for two models.

results:         Simulation results

src:         Stan codes


The following are two questions I met, more information can be found in "summary.pdf":

1. In model1, the performance of FullGP highly depends on initial values. NNGP did not have such a high number of divergent transitions with the same initials and number of iterations as follows. What's more, it converged. I want to compare FullGP and NNGP with initial values far from the true value, but the results from FullGP didn't even converge.  

Initial value: beta = c(0, 0), sigmasq = 6, tausq = 1, phi= 10;

With 400 iterations, I got Warning messages:
1: There were 199 divergent transitions after warm up. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.8 may help. 
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

2. The Full Gaussian Process in model 2 takes a very long time to run. I got 1200 out of 2000 iterations over 10 hours and then my computer stopped running. Hope someone could give me some suggestions on the coding.


Best Wishes,

Lu Zhang

Regarding your question #2, on improving the efficiency of the fullGP models:

First, in your custom function "get_w_L" you should take advantage of the fact that the covariance matrix is symmetric by doing:

    for (j in 1:(N-1)){

            temp_dist[k, j] = temp_dist[j, k] ;
        }
    }
  for(i in 1:N){
  temp_dist[i,i] = sigmasq + tausq ;
  }

You might also be getting into trouble with your priors; for GPs, I follow the guidelines posted at the bottom of the wiki: https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Prior-Choice-Recommendations

And for model fullGP_w.stan, I would rewrite the parameters/model block like follows:
...
parameters {
    vector[2] beta;
    real<lower = 0> sigmasq;
    real<lower = 0> tausq;
    real<lower = ap, upper = bp> phi;
    vector[N] eta;
}
model {
    vector[N] w;
    matrix[N, N] L_cov;
    L_cov = get_w_L(sigmasq, tausq, phi, dist, N);
    sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(as, bs);
    tausq ~ inv_gamma(at, bt);
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    w = mu_w + L_cov * eta;
    for (i in 1:N){
        Y[i] ~ normal((X[i,] * beta + w[i]), tausq);
    }
}



Rob

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: why tau, not tausq
parts:
1.  Inv-gamma has problems (see Gelman, 2006).
2.  tau is more interpretable than tausq.  You can have prior info on tau, it's not so clear how to do that with tausq
3.  Normal dist in Stan uses the normal(mean, sd) parameterization, NOT normal(mean, var).
That pretty much covers it!
On Sep 10, 2016, at 8:46 PM, Lu Zhang <Lu.Z...@ucla.edu> wrote:

Thank you! Actually, the parameter I put is tausq, not tau. I am not very clear why I should set a prior for tau instead of tausq. Is there any beneficial I can get from doing that?
 

On Sat, Sep 10, 2016 at 5:39 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

> On Sep 10, 2016, at 8:01 PM, Rob Trangucci <robert.t...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> And for model fullGP_w.stan, I would rewrite the parameters/model block like follows:
> ...
> parameters {
>     vector[2] beta;
>     real<lower = 0> sigmasq;
>     real<lower = 0> tausq;
>     real<lower = ap, upper = bp> phi;
>     vector[N] eta;
> }
> model {
>     vector[N] w;
>     matrix[N, N] L_cov;
>     L_cov = get_w_L(sigmasq, tausq, phi, dist, N);
>     sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(as, bs);
>     tausq ~ inv_gamma(at, bt);
>     eta ~ normal(0, 1);
>     w = mu_w + L_cov * eta;
>     for (i in 1:N){
>         Y[i] ~ normal((X[i,] * beta + w[i]), tausq);
>     }
> }

You could vectorize the loop to

  Y ~ normal(X * beta + w, tau);

As long as Y is a size-N vector and X is an N x 2 matrix.

And rather than defining tau = sqrt(tausq), you can
just make tau a parameter and put a prior on it
directly.

- Bob

Hi Bob,

    I have a question about coding in FullGP_w.stan. In your previous email, you suggested a rewrite of my parameter/model block for FullGP_w.stan:

> ...
> parameters {
>     vector[2] beta;
>     real<lower = 0> sigmasq;
>     real<lower = 0> tausq;
>     real<lower = ap, upper = bp> phi;
>     vector[N] eta;
> }
> model {
>     vector[N] w;
>     matrix[N, N] L_cov;
>     L_cov = get_w_L(sigmasq, tausq, phi, dist, N);
>     sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(as, bs);
>     tausq ~ inv_gamma(at, bt);
>     eta ~ normal(0, 1);
>     w = mu_w + L_cov * eta;
>     for (i in 1:N){
>         Y[i] ~ normal((X[i,] * beta + w[i]), tausq);
>     }
> }

Different from FullGP.stan, FullGP_w.stan includes the spatial random effect "w" in parameter space, so the dimension increases dramatically from 5 to 1005.   But if I use the code above, how should I retrieve "w"? Should I use a transformed parameter block for that? Thank you very much!

Best Wishes,

Lu
On Sat, Sep 10, 2016 at 5:39 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

> On Sep 10, 2016, at 8:01 PM, Rob Trangucci <robert.t...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> And for model fullGP_w.stan, I would rewrite the parameters/model block like follows:
> ...
> parameters {
>     vector[2] beta;
>     real<lower = 0> sigmasq;
>     real<lower = 0> tausq;
>     real<lower = ap, upper = bp> phi;
>     vector[N] eta;
> }
> model {
>     vector[N] w;
>     matrix[N, N] L_cov;
>     L_cov = get_w_L(sigmasq, tausq, phi, dist, N);
>     sigmasq ~ inv_gamma(as, bs);
>     tausq ~ inv_gamma(at, bt);
>     eta ~ normal(0, 1);
>     w = mu_w + L_cov * eta;
>     for (i in 1:N){
>         Y[i] ~ normal((X[i,] * beta + w[i]), tausq);
>     }
> }

You could vectorize the loop to

  Y ~ normal(X * beta + w, tau);

As long as Y is a size-N vector and X is an N x 2 matrix.

And rather than defining tau = sqrt(tausq), you can
just make tau a parameter and put a prior on it
directly.

- Bob

# Introduction:

This is a test folder for implementing Full Gaussian process and Nearest 
Neighborhood Gaussian Process on spatial data in Stan. For more details 
about synthetic data, models, and simulation results, please refer to 
“summary.pdf”.  


# How to run the program:

The language interface to perform the analysis is Rstan. All the executable files 
are in subfolder “projects” and Stan codes are saved in subfolder “src”. To run 
the analysis, open R program in “projects” and set the working directory to be 
the path of this folder. R code in subfolder “projects” will load data and link 
Stan codes with a relative path.

data: Synthetic data and parameters for priors

projects:         Rstan codes for two models.

results:         Simulation results

src:         Stan codes


The following are two questions I met, more information can be found in "summary.pdf":

1. In model1, the performance of FullGP highly depends on initial values. NNGP did not have such a high number of divergent transitions with the same initials and number of iterations as follows. What's more, it converged. I want to compare FullGP and NNGP with initial values far from the true value, but the results from FullGP didn't even converge.  

Initial value: beta = c(0, 0), sigmasq = 6, tausq = 1, phi= 10;

With 400 iterations, I got Warning messages:
1: There were 199 divergent transitions after warm up. Increasing adapt_delta above 0.8 may help. 
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems

2. The Full Gaussian Process in model 2 takes a very long time to run. I got 1200 out of 2000 iterations over 10 hours and then my computer stopped running. Hope someone could give me some suggestions on the coding.


Best Wishes,

Lu Zhang
